chapter: Europe and the Black and Blue years
title: Scott Hamilton and the night he drank at her gig in New Orleans
summary: Humes admires young Scott Hamilton but scolded him about drinking. In New Orleans he drank through a televised fight, reeled on the stand, apologised and promised it would not happen again.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Oh yeah. We had, there's a little player and I hope he's not drinking now. I hear he's not and I hope not.
Little Scott Hamilton. He is one

of the great ones. He's young, and everybody respect s him. And he's coming up and he's doing big things, you know. But honey he would get so high he wouldn't know how to put his horn in his mouth, and I used to talk to him. And I'd say, Scotty, it's sad because you've got such a future, and you're just going to throw it away on a drink of whiskey.
Did he take that from you alright?

Yeah, he said, well alright. But still he'd go on and drink. But I had him working with me one time down in New Orleans and we didn't have to go on until late that night because there was a big fight and everybody was watching the fight on TV, so the man said not to go on until after the fight is over. I said okay. So Scott went back to the bar and he'd be sitting there drinking a mile a minute yacking to the bar tender, and watching the fight. I guess he doesn't realize how much he was drinking. So he got back on the stand and he was reeling and rocking. And I said, this is it. I didn't say nothing to him, but when he got down off the stand he came over to me and he said, 'Helen, I'm just as sorry as I can be'. He said, 'I didn't know I had
